Sharing the work: one circle in Korean shoegaze

Five years after Downfall of the Neon Youth, credits and concert accounts trace shared production, guest vocals and organising—with a connection to Brazil.

BY indiek / 2026-11-05

Downfall of the Neon Youth turned five on October 22, 2026. The split album brings together contributions from three projects: Parannoul, Asian Glow and sonhos tomam conta. That last name belongs to Lua Viana, whose artist profile lists São Paulo, Brazil. This starting point for exploring a circle around Korean shoegaze already reaches beyond Korea. [Original release](https://longinusrecordings.bandcamp.com/album/downfall-of-the-neon-youth); [Longinus artist profiles](https://longinusrecordings.com/pages/news); [Viana’s projects](https://linktr.ee/sonhostomamconta) and [Bandcamp profile](https://sonhostomamconta.bandcamp.com/album/pesadelos). [1] [2] [4] [5]

The credits show the billed musicians taking several roles. Music and mixing are credited to Parannoul, Gyungwon Shin and Lua Viana. Shin is Asian Glow, identified as Shin Gyungwon in James Gui’s reporting for Pitchfork; Viana also mastered the record. These album-level credits do not explain each song’s division of labour. Sharing a split release does not, by itself, mean that every song was jointly written. [Downfall credits](https://longinusrecordings.bandcamp.com/album/downfall-of-the-neon-youth); [Gui’s reporting](https://pitchfork.com/features/article/parannoul-and-the-new-generation-of-korean-indie/). [1] [3]

On the 2022 joint project Paraglow, Parannoul and Asian Glow—the two musicians who appeared alongside sonhos tomam conta on the split—share production and mixing credits. Here, their names sit together against responsibility for producing the record, although the credits do not specify who played each part or how they exchanged ideas. [Paraglow credits](https://paraglow.bandcamp.com/album/paraglow). [6] [1]

On Della Zyr’s Nebulous You, released in December 2022, Parannoul takes a guest role, contributing vocals to tracks one, two and four. A separate acknowledgment thanks Ian Lim, Wapddi, BrokenTeeth and Asian Glow for “moral support & quality assurance”. It does not describe what that support involved. [Nebulous You credits](https://dellazyr.bandcamp.com/album/nebulous-you). [8]

The same circle also shared the work of putting on a concert. In his 2024 Pitchfork report, James Gui describes Asian Glow suggesting a showcase for their solo projects to Wapddi’s Yang Jihoon, who pursued the idea. According to Longinus Recordings’ participant account, Digital Dawn took place in Seoul on August 14, 2022. The label credits Wapddi with organising it, helped by the performing artists and, to a lesser extent, Longinus itself. [Gui’s scene report](https://pitchfork.com/features/article/parannoul-and-the-new-generation-of-korean-indie/); [Longinus’s Digital Dawn account](https://longinusrecordings.com/pages/news). [3] [2]
